title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the comparison theorem ('Théorème bis', (39)) from the previous page. On that page Grothendieck builds a group SM_{ρ,σ} as a fibre product. Its elements are pairs (x, u), where x lies in a group M_{ρ,σ} of 'symmetries' and u lies in a group B'_0. SM_{ρ,σ} is an extension of M_{ρ,σ} by L_0, and it splits as a semi-direct product SM ≅ M·L_0 once a splitting is chosen. The page fits Grothendieck's programme of describing Galois–Teichmüller-type groups through solution sets of 'loop equations' in fundamental groups. In that setting ρ, σ index two elementary 'symmetry' or loop data, and G is the group of the target object.

(40) makes the isomorphism of (39) explicit. Each x gives three images: a = θ_ρ(x) in T_ρ, b = θ_σ(x) in N'_σ, and U = θ_G(x) in G. The pair (x, u) is sent to the triple (α, β, f) = (u a^{-1}, u b^{-1}, u U^{-1}). This triple is a solution of the system (37)+(31), i.e. a point of S Σ*_{ρ,σ}. Grothendieck exclaims 'comme c'est beau !'.

(41) L_0 acts on the solution set Σ_{ρ,σ} by simultaneous left multiplication, (α, β, f) ↦ (lα, lβ, lf). Under (40) this is left translation of SM_{ρ,σ} by elements (1, l) with l in L_0. Passing to the quotient by L_0 therefore recovers ('en principe') M_{ρ,σ} ≅ SM_{ρ,σ}/L_0 as the space of solutions of Σ*_{ρ,σ} modulo the L_0-action.

Remark. The essential quantities are u, a, b, U, which suggests the morphism (42): SM_{ρ,σ} → B'_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ × G, (x, u) ↦ (u, a, b, U).

Proposition. (42) is a monomorphism. Its image consists of the systems with det u = det b = det U =: μ and det a / μ ∈ Γμ_n (43). Here 'det' is presumably an abelianization- or cyclotomic-type character to an abelian group, and μ_n a cyclic group of roots of unity. The proof is said to follow at once from the corollaries on p. 536' and from the fibre-product definition of SM.

So the page gives a 'graph' description: a group of Teichmüller-type symmetries is embedded into a product of four concrete groups, cut out by determinant compatibilities. The next page uses this to define sub-groups M_{ρ,σ}(σ) by U = b and M_{ρ,σ}(ρ) by U = a, which are partial sections over T_ρ ×_{μ_n} N'_σ.
errors: The injectivity claim in (42) and the exact form of (43) cannot be checked independently; they depend on unseen definitions (p. 536', (31), (37)). The page offers no proof beyond 'conséquence immédiate'.
Grothendieck is not consistent about whether the target set is Σ_{ρ,σ}, Σ*_{ρ,σ} or SΣ*_{ρ,σ}. The L_0-quotient statement is hedged with '(en principe)'.

ideas.what: Explicit isomorphism from a fibre-product group SM to the set of solutions (α, β, f) of loop equations via α = u a^{-1}, β = u b^{-1}, f = u U^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Description of a GT-type group (Grothendieck–Teichmüller variants) as a solution set of loop/pentagon-hexagon type equations; torsor/trivialization description
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT via (λ, f) equations; Ihara, Schneps, Lochak and others for variants
ideas.where_published: Only the programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme; the detailed 'équation des lacets' work is unpublished

ideas.what: Left L_0-action on solutions corresponds to left translation in SM; M ≅ SM/L_0
ideas.modern_name: Quotient of an extension by its kernel; torsor structure on the solution set

ideas.what: Embedding SM_{ρ,σ} → B'_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ × G with image cut out by determinant (character) compatibilities
ideas.modern_name: Graph embedding of a fibre product, with image described by abelianized/cyclotomic character conditions

missed.claim: The page is part of an unpublished, detailed and fairly finished study of groups M_{ρ,σ}. These are Teichmüller-type symmetry groups described by loop equations together with an explicit 'universal' extension SM_{ρ,σ}. The study includes a concrete embedding into a product of four groups with determinant conditions. To my knowledge no published GT-variant literature records this in this form.
missed.quote: L'homom. (42) est un monom., son image est formée des systèmes satisfaisant (43) det u = det b = det U soit μ, et det a/μ ∈ Γμ_n
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may give an alternative, more 'linear' presentation of GT-like groups attached to symmetries of order ρ, σ. Such a presentation could be compared with Schneps' and Lochak's variants of GT. The significance is unclear without the surrounding definitions.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is technical bookkeeping inside a larger unpublished development: an explicit isomorphism, a quotient by L_0, and an injectivity proposition with determinant conditions. The individual steps are routine. The only interest is that the surrounding 'équation des lacets' programme is unpublished.
transcription_corrections: In (42) the third factor of the target is N'_σ (as on the next page), not T'_σ: B'_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ × G.
Line under (40): '(comme c'est beau !)' — the reading is plausible.
'transfo[?] à gauche' is likely 'translation à gauche'.
'formulé[?] des (1, l)' is likely 'formée des (1, l)', i.e. the left translations by the elements (1, l) with l ∈ L_0.
'cor. à la page de p. 536'' is likely 'cor. à la prop. de p. 536''.
